reference_use.conclusion: The pinned SimonGMT has covectors, forms, test forms, currents and covectorEuclideanNorm. It has no continuity lemma for pulled-back forms and no mollification of covector-valued fields. Its convolution code (Chapter02/BV, WhitneyPartition, Chapter08) is scalar and not imported by the contract. No DAG declaration has the three child types. The nearest accepted ones work in covectorEuclideanNorm: dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field (needs |g| ≤ 1, fixed ε) and part (d) of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (bound on |ξ(α)|). So all three children are new, and the names dtc_bc_lc_pf_ext_* are unused in dag.json and git history. The frozen imports exclude ContDiffBump.normed, so the mollification normalizes the bump by hand and uses dist_convolution_le, as the accepted candidate 8abce32 does. Measurability of ξ(G) needs Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ with isBoundedBilinearMap_apply. All three types elaborate in the comparator scope, and complete Lean proofs of all three use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The exact frozen parent type is proved in Lean from them plus the carrier_facts dependency; the only sorry is the placeholder for that queued dependency.

proof:
Source: steps 4–6 of the parent proof. They identify ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ with the limit of the integrals against uniformly approximating forms, as behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 415–424) for currents with the integral representation 2.7 (line 271). Three generalizations: the carrier fact Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0 with spt Y ⊆ K is replaced by the hypothesis Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0; the specific forms ω_j, h are replaced by arbitrary continuous g_j, g with g_j → g uniformly on K; and ℝ^P is replaced by an arbitrary U ⊇ K.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]. M := R.carrier, a measurable set. θ := R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ, measurable. ξ := R.orient; ξ(x) ∈ MultiVector P n is a continuous linear functional on Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n. μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Λⁿ. F_j(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(g_j(x)) and F(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)). The claim is ∫F_j dμ → ∫F dμ, i.e. ∫_M θξ(g_j) dHⁿ → ∫_M θξ(g) dHⁿ.
1. μ-almost every point lies in K. Since M is measurable (R.measurableSet_carrier), ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ K is equivalent to Hⁿ{x : x ∈ M and x ∉ K} = 0 (ae_restrict_iff', ae_iff). That set is M ∖ K, which is Hⁿ-null by hypothesis.
2. Orientation bound. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. So there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) in ℝ^P with either ξ(x)(β) = β(τ) for all β ∈ Λⁿ, or ξ(x)(β) = −β(τ) for all β. At such x, for every β ∈ Λⁿ: |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; ‖τ_i‖ = 1 by orthonormality; for n = 0 the empty product is 1). Hence ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ β ∈ Λⁿ, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖.
3. θ is μ-integrable. Since K is compact and K ⊆ U, R.locallyIntegrable_mult gives c := ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. We have M ∖ (M ∩ K) = M ∖ K, which is Hⁿ-null, and (M ∩ K) ∖ M = ∅. So M and M ∩ K agree Hⁿ-a.e. (ae_eq_set), and μ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_congr_set). The function x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) ≥ 0 is measurable (measurable_from_nat composed with R.measurable_mult), and ‖(θ(x) : ℝ)‖ₑ = θ(x) (Real.enorm_natCast). So ∫⁻ ‖θ‖ₑ dμ = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ = c < ∞, and θ is μ-integrable (HasFiniteIntegral). Put Θ := ∫ θ dμ, a real number with Θ ≥ 0.
4. Measurability. Let G : ℝ^P → Λⁿ be continuous. Then x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(G(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, because:
 - x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable;
 - ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient);
 - G is continuous, hence strongly measurable;
 - the evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β), MultiVector P n × Λⁿ → ℝ, is bounded bilinear, hence continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply), so x ↦ ξ(x)(G(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂);
 - a product of a.e. strongly measurable real functions is a.e. strongly measurable.
 Lean remark: use Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ with isBoundedBilinearMap_apply, as the accepted cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub does. ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ does not unify with R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, because the topology instance on MultiVector P n differs syntactically.
5. Integrability. Let G : ℝ^P → Λⁿ be continuous. G is continuous on the compact set K, so there is C_G with ‖G(x)‖ ≤ C_G for x ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). For μ-a.e. x, x ∈ K (step 1) and the bound of step 2 holds. At such x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(G(x))| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(G(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖G(x)‖ ≤ C_G·θ(x). The function C_G·θ is μ-integrable (step 3), so with step 4, x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(G(x)) is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono'). In particular every F_j and F is μ-integrable, since g_j and g are continuous.
6. Estimate. Let ε > 0 and put ε' := ε/(Θ + 1) > 0. Since g_j → g uniformly on K, there is J such that ‖g_j(x) − g(x)‖ = dist(g(x), g_j(x)) < ε' for all j ≥ J and all x ∈ K (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff). Fix j ≥ J. For μ-a.e. x (x ∈ K and the bound of step 2 holds), linearity of ξ(x) gives
 |F_j(x) − F(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(g_j(x) − g(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖g_j(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·ε'.
 Since F_j and F are μ-integrable (step 5), ∫F_j dμ − ∫F dμ = ∫(F_j − F) dμ (integral_sub). With the integrable bound θ·ε' (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le), |∫F_j dμ − ∫F dμ| ≤ ∫ θ·ε' dμ = Θ·ε/(Θ + 1) < ε (integral_mul_const; Θ ≥ 0).
7. So for every ε > 0 there is J with |∫F_j dμ − ∫F dμ| < ε for all j ≥ J. By Metric.tendsto_atTop, ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g_j(x)) dHⁿ(x) → ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)) dHⁿ(x) as j → ∞. ∎
key_steps: Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 implies μ-a.e. x ∈ K and μ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K); R.locallyIntegrable_mult on K then makes θ μ-integrable with Θ = ∫θ dμ < ∞.
R.orients gives |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ for μ-a.e. x (orthonormal τ, le_opNorm).
For continuous G, θξ(G) is a.e. strongly measurable (evaluation is bounded bilinear) and bounded a.e. by (sup_K ‖G‖)·θ, hence integrable.
Uniform convergence on K gives |∫θξ(g_j) − ∫θξ(g)| ≤ ∫θ‖g_j − g‖ ≤ Θ·ε/(Θ+1) < ε for large j.
